rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Moses–Pharaoh exchange, the singular نعمة denotes an earthly favor, not bliss in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهي أيضاً نعمة في الدنيا لا الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural نعم and أنعم describe the blessings God grants people in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وكذلك جاء الجمع منها: نعم، وأنعم فيما ينعم الله به على عباده في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نعْماء is likewise used specifically for worldly comfort, as in the relief after hardship in Hud.
rows.anchor: ونعماء أيضاً، جاءت خاصة بالدنيا في آية هود 10

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her survey finds نعيم consistently reserved for afterlife bliss, unlike نعمة and its related forms, which denote worldly gifts.
rows.anchor: اطرد كذلك كجئ "نعيم" خاصاً بالآخرة، في كل الآيات التي ورد فيها لفظ نعيم بالقرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Quranic usage consistently gives نعيم an afterlife sense, this verse should be read by that Quranic usage rather than a possible worldly or figurative meaning.
rows.anchor: وأما هذه الدلالة القرآنية لكلمة "النعيم" خاصة بنعيم الآخرة، في كل المواضع التي ذكر فيها النعيم في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She says the interpreters she read list many mixed explanations but omit the specifically Quranic sense of نعيم as afterlife bliss.
rows.anchor: هو الوحيد الذي لم يذكره المفسرون - فيما قرأت - وهم يعدون كل ما يمكت أن يقال في تفسير النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those absorbed in wealth and children mistake transient worldly goods for ultimate bliss; at judgment they will be asked about the true, lasting bliss of the afterlife they neglected.
rows.anchor: إنما هو عن نعيم الآخرة.... وسر البيان فيه، أن هؤلاء الذين ألهالهم التكاثر في الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Health, wealth, shade, water, food, shelter, and clothing are temporary worldly gifts, not the true bliss about which the people will be questioned.
rows.anchor: لا عن الأعراض الزائلة، من صحة ومال وظل وماء ومأكل ومسكن، وثياب ونعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife reading coheres with the surah’s warning throughout; rival readings disrupt its connected sequence and rhetorical unity.
rows.anchor: والإنذار بهذا السؤال عن النعيم، يتسق على أكمل وجه، مع الوعيد المسيطر على السورة كلها

none: Verse text and surah heading only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar name is Surat al-Alaq; al-Tabari calls it Surat Iqra or Iqra bi-smi rabbik, while al-Razi calls it Surat al-Qalam, a name easily confused with the following surah, which he calls Nun.
rows.anchor: المشهور في اسمها: "سورة العلق" ويذكرها بعض المفسرين، كالطبري باسم "سورة اقرأ"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She presents the surah’s opening as the first revelation, noting that Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari report no disagreement about that account.
rows.anchor: والمشهور كذلك أنه أمل سورة نزلت من الوحي. ولم يشر "ابن إسحاق" في (السيرة النبوية) إلي خلاف

rows.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
rows.claim: Aisha recounts Muhammad’s true dreams, retreat to Hira, Gabriel’s command and three embraces, and the recitation of the opening five verses, which remained fixed in his heart; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن "السيدة عائشة أم المؤمنين" قالت: "كان أول ما ابتدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي

rows.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
rows.claim: Aisha continues that Muhammad saw Gabriel in the sky, returned to Khadija, and was reassured because his character included kinship, truthfulness, trustworthiness, hospitality, and helping in adversity; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: فقالت: أبشر يا ابن عم واثبت، فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبداً، إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث

rows.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
rows.claim: After hearing Muhammad’s account, Waraqa identifies him as the prophet of this community and bearer of the revelation given to Moses, predicts rejection and persecution, and wishes he could support him; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: فقال: والذي نفسي بيده إنك لنبي هذه الأمة، ولقد جاءك الناموس الأكبر الذي جاء موسى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري والفخر الرازي
rows.claim: An alternative view in al-Kashshaf and al-Razi’s commentary makes the Fatiha the first revealed surah, followed by al-Alaq.
rows.anchor: ولكن هناك قولاً - في الكشاف وتفسير الرازي - أن الفاتحة كانت أول سورة نزلت من الوحي

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi also transmits that only al-Alaq’s first five verses came at the start; the remainder came after public opposition and were joined to the surah by God’s command.
rows.anchor: أن الذي نزل من السورة أول الوحي، آياتها الخمس الأولى

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit says the surah is Meccan and its opening was the first revelation at Hira, as established in Bukhari and elsewhere; it judges the claims that al-Muddaththir or the Fatiha came first unsound.
rows.anchor: وقول جابر: أول ما نزل المدثر، وقول أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل: أول ما نزل الفاتحة، لا يصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports in al-Tabari and the Prophetic biography stop the first-revelation account at verse five, supporting the view that the opening alone was first revealed.
rows.anchor: حيث يقف الحديث فيهما عن اول ما نزل من الوحي، عند الآية الخامسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening command to recite is striking because it begins revelation to an unlettered Prophet among an unlettered, pagan Bedouin people, with the Book as his miracle.
rows.anchor: أن تكون كلمة {اقْرَأْ} أول ما استهل به الوحي إلى النبي الأمي المبعوث في الأميين رسولاً منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interpret the early surah through what its first hearers understood, rather than later additions to its meaning.
rows.anchor: ونحتاج هنا في هذه السورة المبكرة من أول الوحي، إلى تمثل ما كان لها

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari did not allegorize the command because its ordinary Arabic meaning, reciting from a written or unwritten text, was clear; Arabs knew rabb as owner and object of worship.
rows.anchor: لم يجد حاجة إلى تأويل آية: {اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ} لوضوح معناها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to recite in the name of the Creator, the rightful Lord rather than the idols the Arabs had fashioned and then worshiped.
rows.anchor: فباسم ربه الذي خلق، أمر المصطفى أن يقرأ. وقد كان لقبائل العرب الوثنية أربابها من أوثان وأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding religious scene was dark: northern Arabian Jews had forgotten Moses and worshiped gold, Syrian and Najrani Christians were divided, and Magians worshiped fire.
rows.anchor: والنصارى - في الشام ونجران - قد مزقتهم التفرقة المذهبية، فبعضهم لبعض عدو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the solitary seeker at Hira, the first revealed words guided him to the truth he sought and ended his long uncertainty like a new dawn.
rows.anchor: توجيهاً وهداية إلى الحق الذيى طال التماسه إياه، وإذاناً بانتهاء حيرته

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi takes the command to recite in God’s name as implying that every Quran recitation should begin with God’s name.
rows.anchor: في قوله: {اقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ} إشعاراً بأن كل قراءة القرآن يجب أن تبدأ باسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She hesitates over al-Razi’s distinction that rabb is an attribute of action whereas Allah is an essential name, with worship here commanded through the former.
rows.anchor: أن الرب من صفات الفعل والله من أسماء الذات.... فالأمر هنا يستوجب العبادة بصفات الفعل

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says Rabbika comforts the Prophet: God has nurtured him from an embryo into a knowing believer, so he should neither fear nor expect abandonment; the command also obliges him to act.
rows.anchor: ما يزيل فزع الرسول من الوحي. فكأنه قال: ربك هو الذي رباك فكيف يفزعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She centers Rabbika on the Prophet’s long search for guidance: the Creator revealed Himself as the Lord worthy of worship over created Arabian idols.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو نور الكلمة يشرق فيهديه إلى ربه الذي خلق، الجدير بالعبادة دون هذه الأرباب المخلوقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects supplying an unstated object for خلق and keeps the first verse’s creation unqualified; the following verse then specifies the human being.
rows.anchor: ولا وجه عندنا لما تعلق به بعض المفسرين من تأول مفعول لـ {خَلَقَ} في الآية الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verse states creation generally, while the next specifies the human, recipient of revelation and the one uniquely able to read, learn, and bear religious responsibility.
rows.anchor: تخصيص هذا العام، باللفت إلى خلق الإنسان، من حيث كان الوحي القرآني لهداية هذا الإنسان

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Razi transmits an argument that naming God as Creator leads idolaters gradually to acknowledge Him: they know they did not create themselves and that their handmade idols did not create them.
rows.anchor: فقدم تعالى في {الَّذِي خَلَقَ} مقدمة تلجئهم إلى الاعتراف به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context plainly asserts the Creator’s lordship; humans are singled out because they read, learn, bear obligations, and receive the revealed words.
rows.anchor: وسياق الآيات صريح في أنه تقرير لربوبية الخالق. وتخصيص خلق الإنسان بالذكر دون سائر المخلوقات

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities read the human’s creation from a clot as reassurance that the Lord who summoned and nurtured Muhammad had cared for him from that earliest stage.
rows.anchor: من السلف من تأويله على أن المقصود به إيناس الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام إلى ربه الذي دعاه ورباه

rows.speaker: آخرون من السلف
rows.claim: Other early authorities take the mention of the clot as a gradual argument bringing idolaters to acknowledge their Creator, as in al-Razi’s account.
rows.anchor: وآخرون منهم تأولوه على قصد التدرج بعباد الأوثان إلى الإقرار بخالفتهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the verse magnifies human creation and displays its remarkable constitution; al-Razi adds that moving from lowly clot to noble knowledge requires a directing Maker.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري إن في الآية تفخيماً لخلق الإنسان ودلالة على عجيب فطرته

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says Rabbuka comforts Muhammad and identifies his exclusive Lord; the Creator attribute follows because Arabs called idols lords, though idols cannot create.
rows.anchor: ذكر {رَبَّكُ} في الآية الأولى، إيناس للمصطفى وتعيين لربه، لا رب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects modern embryology as the verse’s intended lesson: its first audience had no conception of that science, and the Quran would not offer an unintelligible sign.
rows.anchor: وغير متصور أن يكون القرآن الكريم قدم لهم من آيات ربوبية الخالق وقدرته، ما لا سبيل لأحد منهم إلى تصوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, علق can mean material things that cling or adhere, such as blood, and figuratively an attachment or bond of love or hatred.
rows.anchor: والعربية قد استعملت العلق مادياً في كل ما يعلق وينشب: كالدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar expression علقت المرأة means that a woman became pregnant; علق here is the plural of علقة and preserves the generic scope of الإنسان.
rows.anchor: وهم الذين ألفوا استعمال: علقت المرآة، بمعنى حملت. واستعمال العلق هنا، جمع علقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is a sign of human creation, knowledge, and moral responsibility, followed by the human’s delusion of independence and forgetfulness of return to God.
rows.anchor: وإنما هي آية الله في هذا الإنسان، خلقه من علق، وخصه بالعلم، واحتمل أمانة التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first revelation briefly sketches humanity’s whole story from origin to end, a sketch expanded in later revelations.
rows.anchor: وهذه هي قصة الإنسان، من المبدأ إلى المنتهى، تلفت إليه سورة الوحي الأولى، بإيجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Passages revealed later trace humanity from creation through death and resurrection, linking human origins to accountability and return.
rows.anchor: هذا الإنسان الذي خلق الله من علق، وعلمه ما لم يكن يعلم، وإليه رجعاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These creation passages do not direct readers to embryology; they argue that the Creator can raise people again for judgment, reward, punishment, and religious responsibility.
rows.anchor: وما من آية فيها، يؤذن سياقها بتوجيه إلى النظر في علم الأجنة وعلم الأحياء والتشريح

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes, as al-Razi transmits, say the first اقرأ is for the Prophet himself and the second for proclamation to others.
rows.anchor: أن {اقْرَأْ} في الآية الأولى تعني: "اقرأ لنفسك، وهي في هذه الآية بمعنى التبليغ

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A second reported interpretation makes the first command to read for learning and the second to teach.
rows.anchor: أو أن الأولى للتعلم، والثانية للتعليم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A third reported interpretation says the first recitation is in prayer and the second outside prayer.
rows.anchor: أو أن الأولى: اقرأ في صلاتك، والثانية: اقرأ خارج صلاتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She prefers the straightforward context: the command to recite is reiterated, and revelation specifies what the Prophet should read in his Lord’s name.
rows.anchor: وهي أقوال متقاربة، وإن كان الأولى لأخذ السياق على ظاهره، بما يفيد من تأكيد الأمر الإلهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, karam is the opposite of baseness and suggests honor; ikram is the opposite of humiliation and degradation.
rows.anchor: والكرم في العربية نقيض اللؤم، ودلالته على العزة مألوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran applies karim to God, His throne, a messenger, an angel, scripture, and the promised provision, reward, abode, and station of the righteous.
rows.anchor: كما جاء وصفاً لرسول، وملك، وكتاب، وقرآن كريم، ووعد المتقون برزق، وأجر، ومدخل ومقام كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a threatening, ironic address to the sinner, the Quran calls him العزيز الكريم as he is led to Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي سياق الوعيد والسخرية، جاءت آية الدخان في الأثيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s honoring of the righteous is contrasted with His humiliating whom He wills; in al-Hujurat, akramakum is restricted to the addressed human community.
rows.anchor: أما أفعل التفضيل، فجاء مرة مضافاً إلى ضمير المخاطبين في آية الحجرات

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains al-Akram as God’s unsurpassed generosity: He gives countless gifts, is patient with disbelief, accepts repentance, and forgives grave sins.
rows.anchor: الذي له الكمال زيادة كرمه على كل كرم، ينعم على عباده النعم التي لا تحصى

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says God not only forbears when people sin but increases His kindness afterward; a cited poem makes the point that greater failure brings greater favor.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى لا يحلن وقت جناية الإنسان فحسب، بل يزيد إحسانه بعد الجناية

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi’s second explanation contrasts Muhammad’s generosity with the greater generosity of his Lord.
rows.anchor: أنك كريم يا محمد، لكن ربك الأكرم

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi also says God originates every generosity and kindness, and His generosity is free of any shortcoming.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى له الابتداء في كل كرم وإحسان، وكرمه غير مشوب بتقصير

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: One further reading urges recitation by promising ten rewards for each Quranic letter.
rows.anchor: فهو يجازيك بكل حرف مما تقرأ عشراً

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-Razi reads al-Akram as reassurance to proclaim the message without fear because God will support the Prophet in this strenuous mission.
rows.anchor: تجرد لدعوة الخلق ولا تخف أحداً، فأنا أكرم من أن آمرك بهذا التكليف الشافي ثم لا أنصرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects limiting al-Akram to comparison among finite beings: the definite, unqualified form claims absolute, unrestricted supremacy for God, unlike the human comparison in al-Hujurat.
rows.anchor: والحق أن البيان القرآني حين قيد أفعل التفضيل في آية الحجرات بإضافتها إلى ضمير المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arabic superlative made definite with al and left unspecified conveys an absolute general sense; with a complement or specification, comparison remains limited to that scope.
rows.anchor: أفعل التفضيل معرفاً بأل، وغير مميز، فتفيد من العموم والإطلاق ما لا تفيده الصيغة نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is apprehending a thing as it truly is, and its opposite is ignorance; she had surveyed Quranic uses of knowledge in her commentary on al-Takathur.
rows.anchor: العلم إدراك الشيء على حقيقته، ونقيضه الجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen is the instrument of writing, as in the opening oath of Surat al-Qalam.
rows.anchor: والقلك أداة الكتابة، ومنه آية القلم: {ن وَالْقَلَمِ وَمَا يَسْطُرُونَ}

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari interprets teaching by the pen as teaching humans writing they had not known.
rows.anchor: علم الإنسان الخط بالقلم ولم يكن يعلمه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likewise takes it as writing, which records sciences, wisdom, ancient reports, and revealed books, enabling religion and worldly life to function; Abu Hayyan quotes him.
rows.anchor: وما دونت العلوم ولا قيدت الحكم ولا ضبطت أخبار الأولين ومقالاتهم

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi discusses the honor of the pen and the wisdom in its creation; Ibn Qayyim devotes a chapter to the pen’s rank and benefits.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره الفخر الرازي في شرف القلم وحكمة خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing the preceding discussion of Ibn Qayyim, the author lists his twelve pens, from the primordial decree and revelation through juristic, medical, political, accounting, judicial, testimonial, dream, historical, linguistic, and polemical writing.
rows.anchor: أولها: وأعلاها وأجلها قدراً قلم القدر السابق الذي كتب الله به مقادير الخلائق

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi reads a symbolic sequence: creation from a clot signals rational proofs of divine power and wisdom, while writing by the pen signals revealed evidence, law, and prophethood.
rows.anchor: فكأنها إشارة إلى معرفة الربوبية، والتعليم بالقلم إشارة إلى النبوة

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nishaburi offers an interpretation like al-Razi’s symbolic contrast between rational evidence and knowledge of revelation.
rows.anchor: ومثله النيسابورى في (تفسير غرائب القرآن)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She sets aside symbolic readings and takes the pen as the writing tool that records, preserves, and transmits knowledge across time, place, and generations.
rows.anchor: وحيث لا مجال للإشاريات في منهجنا، نطمئن إلى أن الآية لفتت إلى سر القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran draws an unlettered Prophet and people’s attention to the pen as a Creator’s sign and to acquired knowledge as a human distinction; revelation connects knowledge with Adam’s honor and stewardship.
rows.anchor: بما تعني من اختصاص الإنسان دون سائر الكائنات بالقلم وكسب العلم

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes limit the taught human to Idris or Adam, the first to write with a pen; the author rejects this restriction in favor of the generic human.
rows.anchor: ومن المفسرين من قدر في الآية علمه الله، قيل: هو" إدريس، وقيل آدم لأنه أول من كتب بالقلم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human is an unrestricted species term: God taught humanity all acquired knowledge, without need to specify which knowledge or limit it to a single person.
rows.anchor: بل هو الإنسان، اسماً لعموم الجنس على إطلاقه، علمه الله ما لم يعلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to gloss the verse as teaching writing by the pen; Abu Hayyan judges this to be an explanatory reading.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن "ابن عباس" من أنه قرأ الآية: "علم الخط بالقلم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning turns to the human tendency to become arrogant about knowledge and status among created beings.
rows.anchor: ويمضي البيان القرآني، في الردع المحذر مما يتعرض له الإنسان من غرور بعلمه ومكانه بين المحلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طغيان means exceeding bounds, especially the tyranny of despots; استغناء is the opposite of need, and كلا rebukes and restrains.
rows.anchor: الطغيان تجاوز الحد، وأكثر ما يستعمل في جبروت العتاة المستبدين. والاستغناء ضد الاحتياج

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some interpreters take كلا to mean indeed, arguing that neither preceding nor following material provides anything for a rebuke to address.
rows.anchor: من المفسرين من تأولها بمعنى "حقاً" لأنه ليس قبلها ولا بعدها شيء يتوجه إليه الردع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects reading كلا as merely indeed: it directly precedes human transgression, and the following verses contain ample warning and rebuke.
rows.anchor: فالكلمة متلوة مباشرة بطغيان الإنسان، والآيات بعدها حافلة بما يتوجه إليه الردع والنذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cause is not absorption in money or status; the text says the human imagines himself independent of his Creator and is lured by acquired knowledge into overstepping his place.
rows.anchor: وليس الطغيان عن استغراق في حب المال والجاه كما تأوله بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes take الرجعى to mean return; Abu Hayyan calls it a verbal noun on the feminine faʿla pattern.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن الرجعى هنا بمعنى الرجوع. قال أبو حيان: "الرجعى أي الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She hears in الرجعى the unrestricted endpoint of return, rather than focusing on its grammatical classification as a verbal noun or feminine form.
rows.anchor: ليس ملحوظاً فيها المصدرية ولا التأنيث، بقدر ما يلحظ فيه إطلاق الرجوع إلى غايته القصوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This unique Quranic form warns the deluded human that the ultimate destination and final return are to God; later revelations reiterate that all return to Him.
rows.anchor: ولم تأت صيغة الرجعى في القرآن الكريم إلا في هذه الآية، ردعاً للإنسان المغتر عن طغيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God is linked to human creation from a clot: God is both the beginning and the end, as also stated in Surat al-Layl.
rows.anchor: ارتباطهما بخلق الإنسان من علق، إيذاناً بأن إليه تعالى المبتدأ والمنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the phrases is exclusive: the return is to your Lord and no other, and the first and last belong to God alone.
rows.anchor: إلى ربك، لا إلى غيره، إن لنا، لا لغيرنا

rows.speaker: جمهرة المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes identify the man forbidding prayer as Abu Jahl, who prevented Muhammad from worshiping God.
rows.anchor: وجمهرة المفسرين على ان هذه الآيات، إلى آخر السورة، نزلت في "أبي جهل ابن هشام"

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: A report from al-Hasan al-Basri instead identifies Umayya ibn Khalaf as the man forbidding Salman al-Farisi from praying.
rows.anchor: وفي قول عن الحسن البصري: هو أمية بن خلف، كان ينهي سلمان - الفارسي - عن الصلاة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari recounts Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad at prayer and Abu Jahl’s retreat, saying a trench of fire stood between them; no grading or chain is stated.
rows.anchor: قيل فأتى أبو جهل رسول الله وهو يصلي ليطأ على رقبته فما لبث أن رجع عنه ونكص على عقبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abu Jahl occasion raises a chronological problem for the view that all of al-Alaq was first revealed, before Muhammad had begun preaching or been threatened.
rows.anchor: دون أن يعرضوا لما يرد على هذا، من المشهور في أن سورة العلق هي أول ما نزل من الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing al-Razi’s first solution, the rest of the surah came later about Abu Jahl, and the Prophet was directed to place these verses at its beginning.
rows.anchor: نزلت البقية في أبي جهل بن هشام، وأمر الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بضمها إلى أول السورة

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi’s second solution reads الإنسان generically: despite creation and blessings, people transgress, forget their return, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety.
rows.anchor: أن تحمل الآيات على عموم لفظها في الظاهر، وهو أن الإنسان، جملة الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both explanations are possible; the sequence suggests the passage followed public preaching and prayer, while a specific occasion does not prevent the wording from applying generally.
rows.anchor: وكلا الوجهين جائز. فسياق الآيات في السورة، يشعر بأنها نزلت بعد أن أبلغ المصطفى رسالة ربه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes the conditional clause in verse 13 the second object of arayta in verse 9, treats arayta before the condition as extra, and takes verse 14 as the condition’s answer.
rows.anchor: ذهب الزمخشري في (الكشاف) إلى أن الجملة الشرطية في {أَرَأَيْتَ إِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She objects that this analysis inserts an extra arayta into the flow and leaves an interrogative response unprefixed by fa, contrary to the grammarians’ rule.
rows.anchor: تبدو فيه {أَرَأَيْتَ} في الجملة الشرطية مقحمة على السياق، تمت للزمخشري تسوية الصنعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari’s analysis, holding that arayta’s second object must be an interrogative sentence, a construction frequent in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وكذلك رفض مذهب الزمخشري في جعل {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى} جواباً لشرط {إِنْ كَذَّبَ}

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says an interrogative cannot answer a condition without fa except under poetic necessity, so he rejects al-Zamakhshari’s proposed answer.
rows.anchor: بل نصوا على وجوب الفاء في كل ما اقتضى طلباً بوجه ما، ولا يجوز حذفها إلا في ضرورة شعرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She argues that Quranic interrogative arayta usually omits its second object and directs attention instead to the lesson or warning; she cites several Meccan examples.
rows.anchor: وإنما يستغنى عن هذا المفعول، بتقرير يلفت إلى موضع العبرة والنذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural araytum questions in al-Waqia about human emission, crops, drinking water, and fire follow the same pattern; she also cites other Meccan examples.
rows.anchor: ومثلها السؤال التقريري، خطاباً للجمع، في آيات الواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated arayta in this passage is a stylistic prompt to see and reflect on the warning; it need not take an explicit or inferred second object.
rows.anchor: فلفتت إلى ما هو جدير بالرؤية والبصر والتدبر، وأغنت عما تعلق به النجاة من مفعول ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 14 itself supplies the focal lesson in place of an assumed conditional answer: knowing that God sees is the needed warning, without a hidden answer clause.
rows.anchor: لتكون آية {أَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَرَى} هو موضع العبرة والبصر والتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Quranic conditional questions are followed by interrogatives without fa, including examples in al-Anam, al-Qasas, and Hud.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام فيها في موضع حواب الشرط، غير مقترن بالفاء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says raʾa with two objects can mean knowing, and arayta functions like akhbirni; such questions alert the listener to a warning.
rows.anchor: رأى إذا عدى إلى مفعولين اقتضى معنى العلم. ويجرى {أَرَأَيْتَ} مجرى: أخبرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She urges readers to notice Quranic stylistic patterns even when they depart from school grammar and rhetoric, rather than forcing them into technical rules by conjecture.
rows.anchor: فيشغلنا عن البيان العالى، تسوية الصنعة النحوية أو البلاغية، بالتأويل فيه والتقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سفع can mean striking or forcefully grabbing: a bird smites prey with its wings, and a horseman yanks a horse by its forelock; a line by Amr ibn Maʿdikarib illustrates the latter.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن معد يكرب، - رضي الله عنه -: قوه إذا كثر الصياح رأيتهم من بين ملجم مهره أو سافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is also common for scorching by poisonous heat or flame, as when a blaze sears a face.
rows.anchor: وكثر استعمال السفع في لفح السموم تلطم وجه الملفوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Metaphorically, seizing someone by the forelock means dragging him violently to humiliate and punish him, while signaling the seizer’s power.
rows.anchor: سفع بناصيته، بمعنى اجتذبها بعنف قصد الإذلال والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forelock is the hair at the front of the head and can stand for the face, anything foremost, or the leading people of a community.
rows.anchor: والناصية قصاصة الشعر في مقدمة الرأس. ويستغنى بالناصية مجازاً عن الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سفع occurs only here in the Quran; the forelock elsewhere signifies God’s control in Hud and the humiliation of sinners in al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: أما الناصية فجاءت مرة في آية هود، 56، بمعنى التمكن والاقتدار والتحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s emphatic seizure at the forelock conveys the greatest threat, evoking both dragging the offender to Fire and the blaze scorching him.
rows.anchor: ويقوى هذه الدلالة في آية العلق، مجئُ السفع بالناصية، بفعله المؤكد مسنداً إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the forelock lying and sinful invokes the Quran’s predominant religious sense of disbelief and misguidance.
rows.anchor: بدلالتها الإسلامية الخاصة على الكفر والضلال، وهي الدلالة الغالبة في الاستعمال القرآني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: النادي is the community’s gathering place and, by extension, the assembled people; نداء is the call that summons them.
rows.anchor: والنادي في العربية: مجتمع القوم، كالندى والمنتدى. والنداء: الصوت الداعي إلى التجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related terms denote a gathering and its discourse; Dar al-Nadwa was Quraysh’s council, and النادي may mean the people assembled there by local-place metaphor.
rows.anchor: ومنه دار الندوة بمكة، كانت مجتمع قريش تقضى فيها جليل أمورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses the root for mutual summoning, the Day of Calling, a community gathering, and people’s assembly or social circle.
rows.anchor: وجاء التنادي في آية القلم 21

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes connect the verse to Abu Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad as he prayed at the Kaaba; Abu Jahl boasted that no one in the valley had a larger assembly than his.
rows.anchor: فذكورا أن أبا جهل بن هشان حين توعد المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام أن يطأ عنقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boastful person imagines his clan will support and protect him, so he persists in excess and error.
rows.anchor: معتزاً بقومه، مدلاً ما له في عشيرته من حمى ومنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nadi is the group the deluded man summons for help; all of them are powerless against the mighty angels God summons to punish him.
rows.anchor: مراداً به الجمع الذين يدعوهم هذا الضال المغرور، وهو مظنه أن يؤازروه وينصروه

rows.speaker: بعض اللغويين
rows.claim: Lexicographers disagree on زبانية: some treat it as a plural without singular; Abu Ubayda gives زبنية, al-Kisaʾi زبنى, and al-Akhfash زابن, an active participle for fierce force.
rows.anchor: فقيل إنه جمع لا واحد له. وقال أبو عبيدة: واحده زبنية، وقال الكسائي، واحده زبنى

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash derives a singular زابن from zabn, meaning one of fierce attack; the author cites a poem and Utba ibn Sufyan’s phrase about war pushing and being pushed.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش. واحد الزبانية زابن، اسم فاعل من زبن، بمعنى اشتد بطشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic uses زبانية for rebellious humans or jinn and also for a scorpion’s poisonous horns; religious usage makes them angels charged with tormenting sinners in Hell.
rows.anchor: ونقلت الزبانية إلى المصطلح الديني علماً على الملائكة والموكلين بعذاب الخاطئين في جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse leaves the angels’ manner of punishment unspecified, allowing the imagination to range freely over its terror.
rows.anchor: ولم تحدد الآية صنيع الزبانية، بل تركته على إطلاقه الرهيب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes take the pronoun in do not obey him as referring to Abu Jahl, while the apparent context and the preceding pronouns point to the person who disbelieved and turned away.
rows.anchor: وظاهر السياق عود الضمير على الذي {كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujud means submission; the Quran applies it to the angels’ bow before Adam and to Yusuf’s family falling in prostration before him.
rows.anchor: والسجود في العربية الخضوع، ومنه في القرآن الكريم: سجود الملائكة لآدم بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipful prostration is ancient: Abraham and Ishmael were told to purify the sanctuary for worshipers, and pre-Islamic Arabs also bowed to their idols.
rows.anchor: وفيما يتلو علينا القرآن من نبأ إبراهيم والبيت العتيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam abolished prostration to anything but the Creator and made sujud in prayer the climax of humble worship; mosques take their name from this act, and the Kaaba is al-Masjid al-Haram.
rows.anchor: حتى نسخ الإسلام بنوره ظلام الوثنية وأبطل السجود لغير الخالق، وأخذ السجود دلالته الإصطلاحية على السجدة في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command may refer specifically to prayer-prostration, as some exegetes say, while retaining the broader sense of complete humility shown by Quranic descriptions of the faithful.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص السجود بالذكر في آية العلق، يقبل تأويله بالسجود في الصلاة كما ذهب بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other passages describe believers prostrating at night, upon hearing revelation, and in worship; the Prophet is also commanded to praise God and prostrate.
rows.anchor: وأمر الرسول بالسجود في آية العلق، نظيره ما في آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects Abu Hayyan’s interpretation of اقترب as seek closeness through devotion and prefers its direct sense of nearness: the worshiper is nearest to God while prostrating.
rows.anchor: ولا نطمئن إلى تفسير الأقتراب هنا بالتقرب كما ذهب "أبو حيان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ending with nearness names the worshiper’s highest aspiration; the Prophet’s prostration breaks the proud man’s vanity and answers the human illusion of independence, since God owns both afterlife and first life.
rows.anchor: وإذ يأخذ الأقتراب من الله مكانه ختاماً للآية، وليس بعد القربى من الخالق غاية يطمح إليها العابد الساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage mentions an unnamed interpreter’s concern that a reading undermines moral responsibility and says the interpretation attributed to al-Tabari better fits the wording.
rows.anchor: ورأى فيه ما يخل بالتكليف. كما نقل ما ذكرنا من تأويل الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She rejects al-Zamakhshari’s restriction of the verse to reward in both abodes because the context plainly includes both glad tidings and warning.
rows.anchor: قصر معنى الآية في تفسير الزمخشري على "ثواب الدارين" يمنعه العموم المستفاد من صريح السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without settling the free-will debate, she says God is both origin and destination, provides guidance in worldly life, and people’s response or refusal shapes their final outcome.
rows.anchor: الله سبحانه إليه المصير كما له المبتدأ. وهو تعالى يهيئ لخلقه في الدنيا طريق الحق والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is placed before the first life for meaning, not rhyme: it is better and lasting, and its punishment is more severe and enduring.
rows.anchor: وليس التعلق برعاية الفاصلة هو الذي اقتضى تقديم الآخرة هنا على الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same order appears in al-Duha’s promise to the Prophet and in the threat concerning Pharaoh, where the afterlife precedes the first life.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قدمت الآخرة على الأولى في سياق البشرى للمصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، بآية الضحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this warning, لظى means a pure flame and تلظى means the fire blazes; elsewhere لظى is a name for Hell.
rows.anchor: واللظى في العربية اللهب الخالص، والتلظى تسعر النار واحتدام توقدها
